question: ap1
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Forgetting curves and the spacing effect (borrowed from learning psychology)
ideas.description: Adapt Ebbinghaus-style protocols: give cells one stimulus pulse, wait a variable retention interval, then give an identical test pulse and quantify 'savings' (faster or larger AP-1 target induction by scRNA-seq or live reporters) as a function of interval length and of massed versus spaced training pulses. A genuine memory system should show a quantifiable retention decay constant and an advantage for spaced over massed stimulation, and knocking down specific Fos/Jun family members should selectively flatten that curve.

ideas.title: Read-write-erase head assay (borrowed from magnetic tape storage)
ideas.description: Treat a single AP-1-bound enhancer as a storage bit: use dCas9-Fos/Jun fusions to 'write' the state transiently at a naive locus, remove the writer, then assay persistence of accessibility and transcription over many days, and finally 'erase' with targeted motif disruption or a repressive domain and rewrite. Demonstrating independent, locus-specific write/erase/rewrite cycles separates true storage from continuous instructive signaling.

ideas.title: Counting bits of stimulus history (borrowed from information theory)
ideas.description: Expose cells to many randomized stimulus histories (sequences of cytokine, growth factor or drug pulses), then compute the mutual information between the past input sequence and the present single-cell AP-1 chromatin or expression state to estimate how many bits of history the network retains and for how long. Comparing channel capacity in wild-type versus AP-1 motif-mutant or Fos-degron cells quantifies AP-1's specific contribution to memory capacity rather than to instantaneous response.

ideas.title: Tree-ring autocorrelation across lineages (borrowed from dendrochronology)
ideas.description: Combine an evolving CRISPR lineage recorder with single-cell multiome readout so that each cell's AP-1 accessibility state can be placed on a reconstructed division tree, then measure how the correlation in AP-1 state decays with lineage distance and number of intervening mitoses. Heritable memory predicts correlation that persists over several generations and decays with division number rather than with elapsed wall-clock time.

ideas.title: Pulse-chase dating of the memory carrier (borrowed from isotope geochronology)
ideas.description: Use heavy amino acid labeling of Fos/Jun proteins together with labeled-histone nucleosome turnover measurements at the same loci, chasing both after stimulus withdrawal, to date which molecular layer actually carries the persisting signal. If target-gene memory outlives the labeled AP-1 protein pool but tracks the age of nucleosomes or DNA methylation at AP-1 sites, memory is stored in chromatin that AP-1 merely deposited, a distinction that sustained-expression experiments alone cannot make.
